blocks.prompt: 6. Discuss domain, range, and graph of the function \(f(x) = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\).
blocks.explanation:
Pehchaan: \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) bhi exponential function \(a^{x}\) hai, magar is ka base \(a = \frac{1}{3}\) hai, yani \(0 < a < 1\).
Diya kya hai? Function \(f(x) = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\).
Find kya karna hai? Domain, range, aur graph ki behas aur sketch.
Kaunsa rule? Wahi 1.4.2 ki properties jo Question 5 mein lagi thin; farq sirf yeh ke \(0 < a < 1\) hone ki wajah se function ghatta (decreasing) hai, bilkul Example 8 ki tarah.
Plan: properties ek ek kar ke, phir table aur graph, aur aakhir mein Question 5 se muqabla.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x} = \frac{1}{3^{x}} = 3^{-x}\), base \(a = \frac{1}{3}\).
Maloom karna: domain, range aur graph.
Tareeqa: \(0 < a < 1\) wale exponential function ki properties (1.4.2) ek ek kar ke likhenge aur values ka table bana kar graph banayenge. Har property ke saath ek line ki wajah bhi denge, kyun ke "discuss" ka yahi matlab hai.

Domain
\[\text{Dom } f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\, = \mathbb{R}\]
Kyun: \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) har real \(x\) ke liye define hai; koi value mana nahin. Misaal: \(x = -2\) par \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{-2} = 3^{2} = 9\), aur \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) par \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). Har \(x\) ka ek pakka jawab hai.

Positive hona, continuity aur range
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x} > 0 \text{ for all } x\]
\[x \to -\infty:\ \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x} = 3^{-x} \to \infty\]
\[x \to \infty:\ \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x} = \dfrac{1}{3^{x}} \to 0\]
\[\text{Range } f = \,]0, \infty[\]
Kyun: positive base ki har power positive hoti hai. Baayen taraf (\(x\) bohat negative) \(3^{-x}\) bohat bara ho jata hai; daayen taraf \(\frac{1}{3^{x}}\) bohat chhota. Function continuous hai, to 0 aur \(\infty\) ke darmiyan har value leta hai, magar 0 kabhi nahin.

Intercepts
\[f(0) = \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{0} = 1\]
\(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\); \(x\)-intercept koi nahin.
Kyun: kisi bhi non-zero number ki zero power 1 hai; aur \(f(x) = 0\) ka koi hal nahin kyun ke values hamesha positive hain. Dilchasp baat: \(3^{x}\) aur \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) dono ka \(y\)-intercept ek hi point \((0, 1)\) hai; asal mein har \(a^{x}\) is point se guzarta hai.

Strictly decreasing (aur is liye one-to-one)
Agar \(x_{1} < x_{2}\) ho to
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x_{2}} = \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x_{1}} \cdot \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x_{2}-x_{1}} < \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x_{1}}\]
Kyun: \(x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\) aur base 1 se chhota hai, to \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x_{2}-x_{1}} < 1\). 1 se chhoti cheez se multiply karne par number ghat jata hai. Is liye graph baayen se daayen neeche utarta hai.
Dhyan dein: base 1 se bara ho to function barhta hai, 1 se chhota ho to ghatta hai. Yahi Question 5 aur 6 ka asal farq hai.

Horizontal asymptote
Jab \(x \to \infty\), to \(f(x) \to 0\). Is liye \(y = 0\) horizontal asymptote hai, is dafa daayen taraf.
Kyun: daayen taraf curve \(x\)-axis ke qareeb se qareeb tar hoti jati hai magar use chhooti nahin. Misaal: \(x = 5\) par value \(\frac{1}{243}\), aur \(x = 10\) par \(\frac{1}{59049}\): bohat chhoti, magar zero kabhi nahin. Question 5 mein asymptote baayen taraf tha; yahan daayen taraf hai.

Values ka table aur graph
\(x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2\) par \(f(x) = 9, 3, 1, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{9}\).
Points laga kar smooth neeche utarti curve se joriye (figure dekhiye).
Kyun: \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x} = 3^{-x}\), is liye yeh graph \(y = 3^{x}\) (Question 5) ka \(y\)-axis mein aaina (mirror image) hai: wahan jo value \(x\) par thi, yahan \(-x\) par hai.

Tasdeeq: answer key ki range \(]0, \infty[\) aur \((0, 1)\) se guzarta neeche utarta graph hamare jawab se milte hain. Us ka domain ghalat chhapa hai (neeche box dekhiye). Ek aur check: \(x = 1\) par height base ke barabar, yani \(\frac{1}{3}\); point \(\left(1, \frac{1}{3}\right)\) graph par hai.
blocks.final_answer: Dom \(f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\), Range \(f = \,]0, \infty[\). Graph \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai, \(x\)-intercept nahin, poora \(x\)-axis ke upar hai, strictly decreasing (one-to-one) hai, aur \(x \to \infty\) par horizontal asymptote \(y = 0\) hai.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of f(x) = (1/3) to the power x for x from minus 2 to 6. The curve comes down steeply from the left through (minus 2, 9), (minus 1, 3), (0, 1), (1, 1/3) and (2, 1/9), and approaches the x-axis on the right (asymptote y = 0) without touching it.
answer_figure.caption: Graph of f(x) = (1/3)^x: through (0, 1), decreasing, asymptote y = 0

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key Dom \(f = \,]-\infty, \infty]\) chhapti hai, yani \(\infty\) par band bracket. \(\infty\) koi real number nahin, is liye use kabhi shamil nahin kiya ja sakta. Sahi domain \(]-\infty, \infty[\) \(= \mathbb{R}\) hai (bilkul Question 5 ki tarah). Range \(]0, \infty[\) sahi chhapi hai.
